notes.text: Figma name: Hero with background visual · Props: `layout="split"` or `"left"`, `visual` · Use it for: Campaign and product launch pages that want the Lead Form hero's look without a form

**Background visual (split and left-aligned):** the same graphic as the Lead Form hero (`visual-star.svg` in Images; pass its address as `visual`). With split media it sits behind the image or video, starting 7.5% left of it and 15% above, 165% of its width, the media on top. With left-aligned text the copy keeps a 600px column and the graphic fills the right side, centered top to bottom at 110% of that side's width. The section clips whatever runs past its edges. It is decoration only (`aria-hidden`) and never sits under the copy. Not for centered heroes or heroes on a photo or video, where it would fight the copy or the picture.

**Background visual on phones:** with split media it rises from behind the foot of the image into the space above, and stops short of the copy; with left-aligned text it is hidden, since there is no side to fill.

A plain table of copy: a header row, then rows of text, in a white card. Use it for information that reads across, such as module overviews, plan details, specifications and schedules. It has the same parts as MarketingTable (a header row group and a body row group, each cell labeled with its column on phones) without the photo header, row icons or featured column. To set requirements beside what Qualys offers, use MarketingTable; to compare Qualys with competitors, FeatureMatrix or DetailComparison.
Use: **Table** · When: Plain information in rows and columns, not a comparison: module overviews, plan details, specifications, schedules. `size="compact"` for data; `striped` for long tables.
Table: Table (standard) · First column: Any · Min: 2 columns · Max: 6 columns · Why the max: Each column keeps about 200px for wrapping copy in the content column.
Table: Table (compact) · First column: Any · Min: 2 columns · Max: 8 columns · Why the max: Short values need less room; past what fits at 96px a column, the table scrolls sideways.
**Why a minimum of one:** a comparison needs at least one column to compare against. With none, use a list instead of a table. A Table needs two: with one column it is a list.
